question.prompt: Can you walk me through how you handled data splitting for the support ticket classifier at Northstar Demo Labs to prevent data leakage from near-duplicate examples?

answers.transcript: In this fictional Northstar Demo Labs project, I first normalized ticket text and grouped exact duplicates and near-duplicate templates before any split. I kept all tickets from one customer and duplicate cluster in the same partition. I used a time-based split for training, validation, and a final untouched test period, fitting the TF-IDF vocabulary only on training data. I audited cross-split similarity and manually reviewed suspicious matches. The initial random split gave 92 percent macro F1; after removing leakage the held-out score was 81 percent. I reported the lower result because it better reflected new tickets, then used class-level error analysis on validation data to improve rare categories. I would monitor duplicate rates and drift after deployment.

analysis.summary: The candidate provided a thorough, methodologically sound explanation of how they prevented data leakage during data splitting for the support ticket classifier, addressing near-duplicates, customer grouping, time-based splitting, and post-leakage evaluation.

Used a time-based split and avoided fitting TF-IDF vocabulary on validation/test data.
Transparently reported the drop in macro F1 from 92% to 81% after removing leakage.
